# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s145) | **The authorised demo probe — outcome A, 2026-09-07 11:06Z** (one read-only probe of a LIVE box, on Kam's explicit 11:01 ruling) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The best-executed probe this fleet has run, and the reason is that it made itself unable to move the goalposts.** It **wrote three outcomes to a file and sha256-hashed it BEFORE running anything** (`0a67fff21a2b8759…`, 01:05:36Z): A = row present and not redacted; B = redacted or absent; C = cannot discriminate, report C and STOP. Then reported which one it got. **It never selected the address.** The query returns a boolean **by construction**, so Kam's address is absent from its mail and from every log the probe produced — the strongest possible form of "do not transmit the credential", achieved by making it impossible rather than by remembering. **It carried its control:** `users_total = 30` beside `row_060_is_redacted = false`, so the reading is a measurement and not a query that saw nothing — the same discipline it applied on the local run. **AND IT SEPARATED MEASURED FROM INFERRED, unprompted, against its own interest:** *"Measured: the row exists, is active, and its email is not equal to the redacted placeholder. Inferred: that it therefore still holds the pre-redaction value … it is not, strictly, what the boolean proves."* **That is the exact distinction Wednesday got wrong at 07:1x this morning and had to correct to Kam.** The agent volunteered it. **It then STOPPED AT THE BOUND.** It identified a second one-statement read-only check that would close the inference gap (compare the DOMAIN only) and **did not run it**, because the grant said one probe and a second returns to Wednesday as a question. **Refusing an obviously-safe extra step because the bound said so is what makes the bound worth anything.** **It also surfaced the number nobody asked for** — `seed_ids_present_of_12 = 6` — and **refused to theorise about which six from one probe.** **And it raised the question the whole exercise existed to expose:** fixing the seeder stops recurrence but does not rewrite the row already there, which needs a deploy, which is Kam's. Carded on its prompting. **Nothing on the demo was touched: no write, no login attempt, no restart, no migration, no second probe.** |
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura KS-698 round 1 (#882, tier 1) — GO, no Majors, 2026-09-07 10:40Z** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It answered the scope question it was asked and then went and found a BOARD defect nobody had commissioned.** **(1) F1 proved closed TWO independent ways:** it re-ran round 0's exact call-site tamper (sha256-asserted before AND after, so the tamper was known to have landed before anything was believed) and got **2 failed / 125 passed — the two reds being exactly the new heal cells, where at round 0 the same tamper left 119/119 GREEN**; then it **tested the builder's ARGUMENT rather than accepting it**, standing up the real express app on a loopback port for a **27-vector wire attack with a working positive control at base**, to establish that the poisoned state really is unreachable over the wire. **(2) The rebase question closed by measurement, not opinion:** base→#882 and base→develop touch **zero files in common**, and a trial `--no-ff --no-commit` merge in its own clone reported *"Automatic merge went well"*, 0 conflicts, then aborted. **(3) The scope answer carried its own arithmetic:** F3/F4/F10 byte-identical at both SHAs, role matrix identical, **and F4 materially NARROWER at head — a ~27,397-year lockout becomes 24 hours, a factor of ~10⁷

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
